correctness.rationale: For all integers N>=2 the N critical Fourier rows are orthonormal; after each original-row erasure the row Gram has exactly the pair 1±sqrt(1−|a_j|²) and N−2 unit eigenvalues. Parseval and the geometric-series Dirichlet formula give the exact worst overlap. A parity-specific farthest-sample trigonometric identity and strict derivatives prove midpoint uniqueness. A tight-frame rank-one computation gives the regridded comparison. All boundaries (N=2, grid duplicates, non-grid sites) are covered analytically. Independent numerical matrices passed 6,930 assertions for N=2..34, which corroborate but do not certify the all-N result.

value.rationale: A fixed N-point Fourier grid plus one extra measurement is the minimal-redundancy robust interpolation design against one known-position erasure. The complete all-size maximin optimizer and parity exact constants are meaningful natural spectral design invariants. The N^-2 vs N^-1 lower-bound contrast quantifies an N-factor price of not being permitted to reposition existing nodes; this is not a parameter substitution or arbitrary finite slice. Limits: equal row weights and one erasure.
